name: Event planning
what_example: day-of coordination for weddings and parties

not_yet: Don't take full planning before you've run 5 day-of events.
Don't buy decor, linens or rentals to rent out before your tenth event.
Don't book a date without a signed agreement and a deposit.
crowd.note: Weddings peak in spring and fall. Birthdays, showers and work events run all year.
crowd.basis: Scores, buyer, first $1 and not-yet lines: research/niches/events.json crowd_scores (our judgment from its sources). Best months: EventPlanning.com statistics (spring and fall are the peak wedding seasons; Saturdays in May and October book first).

safety: Every booking gets a written agreement: scope and hours, the deposit, the balance date, cancellation, and what happens if storms or a government order stop the event. Have a local attorney review it.
Clients sign and pay each vendor directly. You coordinate the vendors on their behalf.
If a vendor ever pays you a referral fee, tell the client in writing before they book that vendor, and say so in any post that recommends them.
Get general liability insurance before your first event. Venues often ask for a certificate that names them.
Never buy, carry or resell alcohol for a client. The host, a licensed caterer or the venue handles it. The rules differ by state: check your city and state.
Parks and other public spaces can need a permit (in New York City, for 20 or more people). Ask the venue about tents, open flames and crowd limits, and check your city and state.

safety_sources.says: A sample contract: a non-refundable retainer, cancellation terms, force majeure with rescheduling first, and vendors contract with the client directly while the planner coordinates. Have a local attorney review before use.

safety_sources.publisher: 16 CFR 255.5 (FTC Endorsement Guides), via Cornell LII
safety_sources.says: A connection between the endorser and the seller that the audience wouldn't expect must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.
Most event planners pay $21 to $30 per month for liability coverage; certificates of insurance and additional insureds for venues come at no extra cost.

safety_sources.publisher: California Department of Alcoholic Beverage Control
safety_sources.says: The host must buy all the alcohol in advance; a hired bartender may only be paid for bartending, not for alcohol sales.
Special events permits are required for events where twenty or more people will be present, birthday parties included.

extra.title: Free planning call script (30 minutes)
lines: 1. Thanks for making time. Tell me about the event: the date, the place and roughly how many guests.
2. What's booked so far? Venue, caterer, photographer, DJ or band, florist, cake, rentals.
3. What does the venue require: setup start, end time, an insurance certificate, rules on candles or tents?
4. Is any of it outside? Then we write a rain plan with the venue.

5. Here's how I work: I collect every vendor contract and contact, walk the venue with you, send the final timeline a week before, confirm every vendor that week, and I'm on site from the first setup to the last teardown.
6. My founding price is {founding}. A signed agreement and a deposit hold your date. Want me to send it?

The rehearsal add-on is priced at 2 planning hours as a judgment call: no source gives a price, so check current rates. Work events are quoted at the day-of price.

On site from the first vendor's setup to the last teardown

timeline.about: What the Day-of timeline tool builds from. Wedding order and lengths: Zola's sample reception timeline; wedding vendor arrivals: Zola's sample weekend timeline (vendors not in it are our judgment); party, shower and work event programs: our judgment on EventPlanning.com's run of show method. Every default arrival is printed with (confirm). Parties and showers get a shorter breakdown (45 minutes) and a 90-minute setup lead when no vendor is listed.

sources.says: A sample reception in order: drinks and bites, the newlyweds' entrance, first dance, welcome toast, dinner, speeches, parent dances, party time, cake, bouquet and garter toss, last song, private dance and send-off, over about four hours; adjust dancing and dinner to fit.

For a 5pm ceremony: beauty team at 9am, vendors at the venue for setup at 10am, photographer at 1pm, first look at 2:30pm, wedding party photos at 3:30pm, ceremony musicians and guests at 4:30pm, DJ or band at 5pm, vendor breakdown complete an hour after the exit.
Work backward from the fixed points, add buffers on purpose, one activity per row with one owner, and every vendor and helper gets a copy the day before.
Event day: arrive first, check in every vendor, run the day from the run of show, photograph the setup before guests arrive, then teardown, load-out and a venue walkthrough.
